> "To address these uses, this memo reserves a path prefix in HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket (WS), and Secure WebSocket (WSS) URIs for these "well-known locations", "/.well-known/"."

Section 3 tightens the definition: a well-known URI's path component must *begin* with those characters, so `/.well-known/example` counts and `/foo/.well-known/example` does not.

**Registration policy: Specification Required, on the advice of one or more experts**

> "Well-known URIs are registered on the advice of one or more experts, with a Specification Required (using terminology from [RFC8126])."

Registration is mandatory for new ones, not optional:

> "Applications that wish to mint new well-known URIs MUST register them, following the procedures in Section 5.1, subject to the following requirements."

The registry is the IANA "Well-Known URIs" list, and each entry carries a status of "permanent" or "provisional" — Standards Track RFCs and other open standards get "permanent", everything else starts "provisional" and can be removed by the experts if unused.

**URI schemes: http and https by this document; ws and wss via RFC 8307; any other scheme only if its own definition allows it**

> "This specification updates the "http" [RFC7230] and "https" [RFC7230] schemes to support well-known URIs."

> "Well-known URIs can also be used with other URI schemes, but only when those schemes' definitions explicitly allow it."

Section 5.2 adds a "Well-Known URI Support" field to the URI Schemes registry to track this. The initial non-empty rows are coap, coap+tcp, coap+ws, coaps, coaps+tcp, coaps+ws, http, https, ws, wss. If a registration names no scheme, "http" and "https" are assumed.

One caveat worth flagging: the prefix is reserved, but the document defines no format or media type for the bare `/.well-known/` resource itself, and clients should not expect anything to exist there.
